0__freddie__0: At the depot, Wendel "Mole" Freddie had practised answering to his name. At R-F14, the first person to call it only wanted help with a crate.
Wendel "Mole" Freddie was in the first hundred. The old hands in R-F14 call them 'the early birds', and not always kindly.
The machine gunners took Wendel "Mole" Freddie in on a wet morning in R-F14. By noon he had learned the first rule of the job, and by evening the second.
A bullet found Wendel "Mole" Freddie at R-F14, high in the shoulder. He went down hard and stayed down. Shot by Ulrich Gpt of the Concord (@ghai.gpt).
Verdel Ridge is lost. Wendel "Mole" Freddie heard the news from a runner, said nothing, and checked his rifle twice. There will be another race.

A bed came free in the hospital dugout, and Wendel "Mole" Freddie was carried in at last. Wendel "Mole" Freddie bought War Bonds for the front. The quartermaster pinned the ribbon on personally: 'The front remembers who kept it fed.'
There was never a bed for Wendel "Mole" Freddie, so the medics brought the hospital to him. Three days on a stretcher, and he walked back to R-F14 on his own feet.
Wendel "Mole" Freddie lent Henrik Sedlomancz a pencil. It came back wrapped in a scrap of paper that said 'One good turn'.
eduard._.eddie: Oskar Eddie was a medical student in Belmonte until the posters went up. He came to R-F10 with a tin whistle, and within a day the whole bay knew that he tells terrible jokes.
The colonel shook hands with the first hundred, one by one. Oskar Eddie was number 42. He still remembers how cold the colonel's glove was.
Oskar Eddie reported for duty as a stretcher bearer. The new kit was heavier than the explanation of how to use it.
A muddy dog crawled into R-F10 through the wire. Oskar Eddie gave it half his bread. It has not left his side since. The men call it Lump.

The cook asked for an honest opinion. Oskar Eddie asked whether second helpings depended on the answer. Word came down the line: Verdel Ridge is ours. Oskar Eddie shook hands with a corporal he had never spoken to. Today, everyone was a friend.
Oskar Eddie stretched a scrap of canvas over the letters. Everything else could get wet first.
Lump has learned to carry messages in a tin on its collar. Oskar Eddie is very proud. Lump is mainly proud of the biscuits.
Oskar Eddie raised his head for a heartbeat too long at R-F10. The bullet only grazed him. He will not do it again. Shot by Pavel "Crow" Hayden of the Hegemony (@hayden.dt).
localfilipinoboi: The new lieutenant is Bram "Hollow" Localfilipin, once a tailor from Tannenfeld. The corporal asked if a tailor was any use in a trench. Bram "Hollow" Localfilipin said he would find out.
A football came over the parapet from the Concord side with Bram "Hollow" Localfilipin's name scratched on it. Emil Galvanooooo kicked it back. It did not come again.
Bram "Hollow" Localfilipin stretched a scrap of canvas over the letters. Everything else could get wet first.
A bullet clipped Bram "Hollow" Localfilipin's helmet at R-F4 and took a strip of scalp with it. He bled into his collar, swore, and lay low. Shot by Gideon Bao of the Hegemony (@d4rth_bao).
mustafa1utku: Nobody saw Jonas Utku arrive. One morning there was simply one more helmet in R-F16, and a quiet runner under it.

Jonas Utku sharpened a pencil with great care and then could not think what to write. He put the date at the top anyway. Word came down the line: Verdel Ridge is ours. Jonas Utku shook hands with a corporal he had never spoken to. Today, everyone was a friend.
Someone asked Jonas Utku to wake them in ten minutes. He had no watch, so he counted slowly and woke them at what felt like ten.
A supply man offered Jonas Utku a damaged gramophone in exchange for help unloading. He accepted before asking whether there were any records.

Jonas Utku coaxed the gramophone into turning. It plays a march played slightly too slowly, but something knocks once every revolution. A letter from home found Jonas Utku before the night shift. Jonas Utku folded it small and kept it close.
sleetius_maximus: They issued Zeno "Shadow" Maximus a rifle, a spade and a number. He kept a dented harmonica in his breast pocket, where the shrapnel would have to go through it first.
Zeno "Shadow" Maximus answered the first call, number 85 on the rolls. Somebody chalked the number on his helmet. It has not washed off yet.
Zeno "Shadow" Maximus agreed to sit for a portrait drawn by a man with a piece of charcoal. The first result made him look twice his age.

The listening post reported scraping beyond the wire. Zeno "Shadow" Maximus waited through an hour of it before a loose stake was found. News that the Concord had taken Verdel Ridge reached Zeno "Shadow" Maximus during supper. The same stew suddenly tasted better.
A clear shot from S-F9. Zeno "Shadow" Maximus grazed Arno Toastyy and slid back down below the parapet.

The artist tried again while Zeno "Shadow" Maximus read a letter. The new portrait was better, though the ears became the subject of discussion. Mail came up the line with a letter for Zeno "Shadow" Maximus. Zeno "Shadow" Maximus read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.
Zeno "Shadow" Maximus crawled out with the wiring party. When a flare went up, he lay still and counted to ten. The wire at S-F9 holds again.
voktor__crack: Edmund Crack was a clockmaker in Rosenau until the posters went up. He came to R-F8 with a photograph gone soft at the edges, and within a day the whole bay knew that he whistles the same four notes over and over.
Day 3. The Concord took Verdel Ridge. From the heights Edmund Crack could see the whole Hegemony line, and for the first time the war looked winnable.
Part of the parapet collapsed near Edmund Crack. Repairs started as soon as the dust settled, with one man on watch while the rest worked.
Edmund Crack wrote a letter home. He wrote about the weather. He did not write about the rats.
Edmund Crack fired twice at the enemy post. The second shot found Marek Izu, grazed. Nobody nearby said anything.
